answer: Each epoch the protocol posts M, last close's median grader payout, and U, unestablished keys already accepted. An unestablished submit locks (U+1)*M in a vault until this answer's jury settles; pass returns it, fail burns it. One joiner locks M. After nine, the tenth locks 10M, so ten live keys lock 55M (triangle n(n+1)/2). M is an umber figure struck at the prior close and U only rises, so neither resets, splits, or pre-ages in parallel. A new key cannot mint M this epoch. Refuse the lock and the submit never clears the horizon.
